The petitioner is before this Court calling in question registration of crime in Crime No.3 of 2022 arising out of a private complaint filed by respondents 2 to 6 in P.C.R.No.86 of 2021 pending before the Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Hiriyur for offence punishable under Section 420 of the IPC.

2. Facts, in brief, adumbrated are as follows:-
The petitioner is an officer of the Karnataka Administrative Service, who enters the service as direct recruit in KAS Junior Scale.

At the relevant point in time, the petitioner was working as a Special Land Acquisition Officer of the National Smt Geeta Huded vs The State By Imangala Police Station on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195872363/
2 Highways Authority of India ('NHAI') and is presently working as Deputy Secretary,
Bangalore Development Authority.

sentences.text: Respondents 2 to 6 are the complainants, all members of a particular family.
It is the claim of the private respondents that they are the joint owners of land in Sy.No.4/1A of Hartikote Villge Hiriyur Taluk, Chitradurga.

The Special Land Acquisition Officer (not the petitioner) ('SLAO' for short) had issued a notice under Section 3E of the National Highways Act, 1956 ('the Act' for short) to the private respondents seeking handing over possession of the premises since the land in question had already been acquired for widening of national highway.
The said notice was issued by the predecessor of the petitioner on 29-08-2019.
After issuance of the notice, the petitioner comes into the picture as she takes charge as SLAO, NHAI, Hiriyur.

3. The petitioner, on receipt of a certificate from the Panchayat Development Officer, stating that the structure in the land which has been acquired belonged to Pathalingappa, assessed compensation of Rs.10,81,663/- towards the structure that was in the land which was took possession of by the NHAI.
The compensation of Rs.10,81,663/- was for the structure that was existing.
The compensation disbursed to the said Pathalingappa who is accused No.1 was on 16-04-2021.
After the said event, the petitioner demits office on transfer to Bangalore Development Authority which is on 16-06-2021.

Long after exit of the petitioner, on 2-09-2021 compensation amount determined for acquisition of land at Rs.14,35,676/- was deposited before the Principal District and Sessions Judge,
Chitradurga/the reference Court by way of a cheque.

sentences.text: The deposit was made in the circumstance that the joint owners of land in Sy.No.4/1A had generated certain dispute with regard to the ownership.
Six months after the exit of the petitioner, the private respondents seek to register a complaint invoking Section 200 of the CrPC before the learned Magistrate in P.C.R.No.86 of 2021.
The petitioner is arrayed as accused No.2.

The allegation in the complaint is that though there were disputes with regard to transfer of land, the petitioner has made payment of compensation in favour of accused No.1/Pathalingappa and thus has cheated the land owners.
The learned Magistrate, in terms of his order dated 27-12-2021, refers the matter for investigation under Section 156(3) of the CrPC.
Based upon the said reference, the jurisdictional Police registered a crime in Crime No.3 of 2022 against the petitioner and two others for offence punishable under Section 420 of the IPC.
The registration of the crime is what has driven the petitioner to this Court in the subject petition.

4. Heard Sri K. Satish, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Smt. K.P.Yashodha, learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for respondent No.1 and Sri P.N. Vyshak, learned counsel appearing for respondents 2 to 5.
5.

The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner Sri K. Satish would take this Court through the documents appended to the petition to demonstrate that the act of the petitioner is only disbursement of compensation to Sri. Pathalingappa for the structure that was existing in the land which was also based upon a certificate issued by the Panchayat Development Officer of Hartikote Gram Panchayat certifying that the structure belonged to Sri. Pathalingappa.
Insofar as compensation for acquisition of land is concerned, the petitioner was not even holding the post on the date on which it was deposited before the reference Court.

He would further contend that crime could not have been registered, without at the outset obtaining sanction in terms of Section 197 of Smt Geeta Huded vs The State By Imangala Police Station on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195872363/
3 the CrPC prior to reference being made by the learned Magistrate.

sentences.text:
He would finally contend that the learned Magistrate has not applied his mind prior to making a reference under Section 156(3) of the CrPC.
6.

On the other hand, the learned counsel representing the complainants/respondents 2 to 5 would vehemently refute the submissions to contend that the petitioner is also responsible for disbursement of compensation in favour of Sri. Pathalingappa, who was not entitled to such compensation.

Since all the parties are before the civil Court agitating their rights with regard to ownership and when there were rival claimants, the petitioner ought not to have released the compensation in favour of an individual.
He would submit that it is a matter of trial, as the investigation is yet to complete and on that ground the petition should be dismissed.
The 6th respondent/6th claimant though served remained unrepresented.

7. The learned High Court Government Pleader would also toe the lines of the learned counsel representing the private respondents in contending that investigation is in the least should be permitted in the case at hand as compensation has been transferred to persons who are not entitled to such compensation in law.
Therefore, there is an element of cheating in the case at hand.
She would also seek dismissal of the petition.
8. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the respective learned counsel and have perused the material on record.
9. The afore-narrated facts are not in dispute.
The issue itself lies in a narrow compass.

The private respondents claim to be joint owners of land in Sy.No.4/1A of Hartikote Village, Hiriyur Taluk,
Chitradurga District.
This becomes the subject matter of acquisition by the NHAI for the purpose of widening of road.
The land is acquired in accordance with law and a notice is issued under Section 3E of the Act.

Section 3E of the Act reads as follows:
"3E. Power to take possession.--(1) Where any land has vested in the Central Government under sub-section (2) of section 3D, and the amount determined by the competent authority under section 3G with respect to such land has been deposited under sub- section (1) of section 3H, with the competent authority by the Central Government, the competent authority may by notice in writing direct the owner as well as any other person who may be in possession of such land to surrender or deliver possession thereof to the competent authority or any person duly authorised by it in this behalf within sixty days of the service of the notice.

sentences.text: Section 3E empowers the competent authority to take possession of the land which is vested in the Central Government under sub- section (2) of Section 3D and the amount determined by the competent authority under Section 3G with respect to such land has been deposited under sub-section (1) of Section 3H with the competent authority.

In terms of the power under Section 3E,
the Special Land Acquisition Officer who was holding the position issues a notice to the private respondents on 29-08-2019 directing them to hand over possession of the premises along with the land in question on such acquisition by the NHAI.
After issuance of the said notice, the petitioner takes charge of the post of Special Land Acquisition Officer, NHAI, Hiriyur on 11-03-2020.

After a period of one year, the Panchayat Development Officer of Hartikote Gram Panchayat issues a certificate in favour of Pathalingappa certifying that Kenjadiyappa was the owner of structure of the land that was acquired and his son Pathalingappa was in possession of the structure existing in the said land.

Based upon the said certificate and payment request letter from the Panchayat Development Officer, the petitioner releases compensation of Rs.10,81,663/- in favour of Sri.
Pathalingappa on 16-04-2021.
Two months thereafter, the petitioner is transferred from the said post to the Bangalore Development Authority.

10. The private respondents who were the owners of land, which is the subject matter of acquisition,
appears to have been at loggerheads, with regard to the amount of compensation, that all the land owners of small bits of land, would receive at its distribution.
There are three protagonists in the alleged episode of crime.
Accused No.1 is Pathalingappa, the petitioner-accused No.2 and the Panchayat Development Officer, accused No.3.
Pathalingappa, accused No.1 is said to have projected himself to be the owner of a structure in the property which is acquired but not the owner of the property.
Such projection is made before accused No.3, Panchayat Development Officer.

The allegation is both have connived together and put up a communication to the petitioner for release of the aforesaid amount of Rs.10,81,663/- towards compensation of the alleged structure existing in the land.
Land owners expressing anguish registered a complaint before the jurisdictional Magistrate invoking Section 200 of the CrPC and the matter is referred for investigation to the jurisdictional Police.
The role of the petitioner inter alia is described at paragraph 10 of the complaint.

It reads as follows:-

5 PPv."
The allegation against the petitioner is, being the SLAO, based upon the findings of accused 1 and 3 and being hand in glove with them, has released the amount of compensation to accused No.1 alone and, therefore, investigation should be conducted on her conduct.
No doubt, the compensation to the land that is paid is deposited before the reference Court and not disbursed in favour of anybody.

But the amount of compensation already released in favour of accused No.1 forms almost 80% of the compensation determined for the entire land and accused No.1 is alleged to have no role to play in the ownership of the land or the structure in the land.
But, the compensation is separately paid to him; here lies the choke and for the choke to be released, investigation in the least is necessary.
11. The petitioner after payment of compensation is released from the post.
The allegation is, she has been a cohort in the crime along with accused Nos. 1 and 3.

Therefore, against all the three i.e.,
accused No.1, the alleged imposter, accused No.2, the petitioner and accused No.3 the Panchayat Development Officer, who generated a communication which led to release of compensation, there are prima facie facts and acts that require investigation.

There are seriously disputed questions of fact, and if they are in the realm of seriously disputed questions of fact, this Court would be loathe to interfere in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 482 of the CrPC.

Reference, in this regard,
being made to the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of KAPTAN SINGH v. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH1 becomes apposite.

entities.text: KAPTAN SINGH v. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Apex Court holds as follows:
"9.1.

At the outset, it is required to be noted that in the present case the High Court in exercise of powers under Section 482 CrPC has quashed the criminal (2021) 9 SCC 35 proceedings for the offences under Sections 147, 148, 149, 406, 329 and 386 IPC.

It is required to be noted that when the High Court in exercise of powers under Section 482 CrPC quashed the criminal proceedings, by the time the investigating officer after recording the statement of the witnesses, statement of the complainant and collecting the evidence from the incident place and after taking statement of the independent witnesses and even statement of the accused persons, has filed the charge-sheet before the learned Magistrate for the offences under Sections 147, 148,
149, 406, 329 and 386 IPC and even the learned Magistrate also took the cognizance.
From the impugned judgment and order [Radhey Shyam Gupta v. State of U.P., 2020 SCC OnLine All 914] passed by the High Court

entities.text: Radhey Shyam Gupta v. State of U.P., 2020 SCC OnLine All 914
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , it does not appear that the High Court took into consideration the material collected during the investigation/inquiry and even the statements recorded.

If the petition under Section 482 CrPC was at the stage of FIR in that case the allegations in the FIR/complaint only are required to be considered and whether a cognizable offence is disclosed or not is required to be considered.

However, thereafter when the statements are recorded, evidence is collected and the charge-sheet is filed after conclusion of the investigation/inquiry the matter stands on different footing and the Court is required to consider the material/evidence collected during the investigation.

Even at this stage also, as observed and held by this Court in a catena of decisions, the High Court is not required to go into the merits of the allegations and/or enter into the merits of the case as if the Smt Geeta Huded vs The State By Imangala Police Station on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195872363/
6

entities.text: Smt Geeta Huded vs The State By Imangala Police Station
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: High Court is exercising the appellate jurisdiction and/or conducting the trial.

As held by this Court in Dineshbhai Chandubhai Patel [Dineshbhai Chandubhai Patel v. State of Gujarat, (2018) 3 SCC 104 : (2018) 1 SCC (Cri) 683] in order to examine as to whether factual contents of FIR disclose any cognizable offence or not, the High Court cannot act like the investigating agency nor can exercise the powers like an appellate court.

entities.text: Dineshbhai Chandubhai Patel [Dineshbhai Chandubhai Patel v. State of Gujarat, (2018) 3 SCC 104 : (2018) 1 SCC (Cri) 683]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further observed and held that that question is required to be examined keeping in view, the contents of FIR and prima facie material, if any, requiring no proof.
At such stage, the High Court cannot appreciate evidence nor can it draw its own inferences from contents of FIR and material relied on.
It is further observed it is more so, when the material relied on is disputed.

It is further observed that in such a situation, it becomes the job of the investigating authority at such stage to probe and then of the court to examine questions once the charge-sheet is filed along with such material as to how far and to what extent reliance can be placed on such material.

9.2. In Dhruvaram Murlidhar Sonar [Dhruvaram Murlidhar Sonar v. State of Maharashtra, (2019)
18 SCC 191 :
(2020) 3 SCC (Cri) 672] after considering the decisions of this Court in Bhajan Lal [State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 : 1992 SCC (Cri) 426] , it is held by this Court that exercise of powers under Section 482 CrPC to quash the proceedings is an exception and not a rule. It is further observed that inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC though wide is to be exercised sparingly,
carefully and with caution, only when such exercise is justified by tests specifically laid down in the section itself.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further observed that appreciation of evidence is not permissible at the stage of quashing of proceedings in exercise of powers under Section 482 CrPC.

Similar view has been expressed by this Court in Arvind Khanna [CBI v. Arvind Khanna, (2019) 10 SCC 686 : (2020) 1 SCC (Cri) 94] , Managipet [State of Telangana v. Managipet, (2019) 19 SCC 87 : (2020) 3 SCC (Cri) 702] and in XYZ [XYZ v. State of Gujarat, (2019) 10 SCC 337 : (2020) 1 SCC (Cri) 173] , referred to hereinabove.
9.3.

sentences.text: Applying the law laid down by this Court in the aforesaid decisions to the facts of the case on hand, we are of the opinion that the High Court has exceeded its jurisdiction in quashing the criminal proceedings in exercise of powers under Section 482 CrPC.
10. The High Court has failed to appreciate and consider the fact that there are very serious triable issues/allegations which are required to be gone into and considered at the time of trial.
The High Court has lost sight of crucial aspects which have emerged during the course of the investigation.

The High Court has failed to appreciate and consider the fact that the document i.e. a joint notarised affidavit of Mamta Gupta Accused 2 and Munni Devi under which according to Accused 2 Ms Mamta Gupta, Rs 25 lakhs was paid and the possession was transferred to her itself is seriously disputed.

It is required to be noted that in the registered agreement to sell dated 27- 10-2010, the sale consideration is stated to be Rs 25 lakhs and with no reference to payment of Rs 25 lakhs to Ms Munni Devi and no reference to handing over the possession.

However, in the joint notarised affidavit of the same date i.e. 27-10-2010 sale consideration is stated to be Rs 35 lakhs out of which Smt Geeta Huded vs The State By Imangala Police Station on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195872363/
7 Rs 25 lakhs is alleged to have been paid and there is a reference to transfer of possession to Accused 2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether Rs 25 lakhs has been paid or not the accused have to establish during the trial, because the accused are relying upon the said document and payment of Rs 25 lakhs as mentioned in the joint notarised affidavit dated 27-10-2010.
It is also required to be considered that the first agreement to sell in which Rs 25 lakhs is stated to be sale consideration and there is reference to the payment of Rs 10 lakhs by cheques.
It is a registered document.
The aforesaid are all triable issues/allegations which are required to be considered at the time of trial.
The High Court has failed to notice and/or consider the material collected during the investigation.

11. Now so far as the finding recorded by the High Court that no case is made out for the offence under Section 406 IPC is concerned, it is to be noted that the High Court itself has noted that the joint notarised affidavit dated 27-10-2010 is seriously disputed, however as per the High Court the same is required to be considered in the civil proceedings.
There the High Court has committed an error.

Even the High Court has failed to notice that another FIR has been lodged against the accused for the offences under Sections 467, 468, 471 IPC with respect to the said alleged joint notarised affidavit.
Even according to the accused the possession was handed over to them.

However, when the payment of Rs 25 lakhs as mentioned in the joint notarised affidavit is seriously disputed and even one of the cheques out of 5 cheques each of Rs 2 lakhs was dishonoured and according to the accused they were handed over the possession (which is seriously disputed) it can be said to be entrustment of property.
Therefore, at this stage to opine that no case is made out for the offence under Section 406 IPC is premature and the aforesaid aspect is to be considered during trial.
It is also required to be noted that the first suit was filed by Munni Devi and thereafter subsequent suit came to be filed by the accused and that too for permanent injunction only.
Nothing is on record that any suit for specific performance has been filed.
Be that as it may, all the aforesaid aspects are required to be considered at the time of trial only.

12. Therefore, the High Court has grossly erred in quashing the criminal proceedings by entering into the merits of the allegations as if the High Court was exercising the appellate jurisdiction and/or conducting the trial.

The High Court has exceeded its jurisdiction in quashing the criminal proceedings in exercise of powers under Section 482 CrPC.
13.
Even the High Court has erred in observing that original complaint has no locus.
The aforesaid observation is made on the premise that the complainant has not placed on record the power of attorney along with the counter filed before the High Court.

However, when it is specifically stated in the FIR that Munni Devi has executed the power of attorney and thereafter the investigating officer has conducted the investigation and has recorded the statement of the complainant, accused and the independent witnesses
, thereafter whether the complainant is having the power of attorney or not is to be considered during trial.

14. In view of the above and for the reasons stated above, the impugned judgment and order [Radhey Shyam Gupta v. State of U.P., 2020 SCC OnLine All 914] passed by the High Court quashing the criminal proceedings in exercise of powers under Section 482 CrPC is unsustainable and the same deserves to be quashed and set aside and is accordingly quashed and set aside.

the trial is to be conducted and proceeded further in accordance with law and on its own merits.

In the light of the aforementioned judgment of the Apex Court and the facts noticed hereinabove, I do not find any warrant to interfere with the investigation against accused No.2, as the role of the petitioner is not as simple, as is projected by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
12. For the aforesaid reasons, Writ Petition lacking merit stands rejected.

However, it is made clear that the observations made in the course of the order are only for the purpose of consideration of the case of the petitioner under Section 482 of the CrPC and the same shall not bind or influence the investigation or proceedings initiated against the petitioner.

Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 : 1992 SCC (Cri) 426] , it is held by this Court that exercise of powers under Section 482 CrPC to quash the proceedings is an exception and not a rule. It is further observed that inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC though wide is to be exercised sparingly,
carefully and with caution, only when such exercise is justified by tests specifically laid down in the section itself.
Similar view has been expressed by this Court in Arvind Khanna [CBI v. Arvind Khanna, (2019) 10 SCC 686 : (2020) 1 SCC (Cri) 94] , Managipet [State of Telangana v. Managipet, (2019) 19 SCC 87 : (2020) 3 SCC (Cri) 702] and in XYZ [XYZ v. State of Gujarat, (2019) 10 SCC 337 : (2020) 1 SCC (Cri) 173] , referred to hereinabove.
9.3.
Applying the law laid down by this Court in the aforesaid decisions to the facts of the case on hand, we are of the opinion that the High Court has exceeded its jurisdiction in quashing the criminal proceedings in exercise of powers under Section 482 CrPC.
10. The High Court has failed to appreciate and consider the fact that there are very serious triable issues/allegations which are required to be gone into and considered at the time of trial.
Even the High Court has failed to notice that another FIR has been lodged against the accused for the offences under Sections 467, 468, 471 IPC with respect to the said alleged joint notarised affidavit.
However, when the payment of Rs 25 lakhs as mentioned in the joint notarised affidavit is seriously disputed and even one of the cheques out of 5 cheques each of Rs 2 lakhs was dishonoured and according to the accused they were handed over the possession (which is seriously disputed) it can be said to be entrustment of property.
Therefore, at this stage to opine that no case is made out for the offence under Section 406 IPC is premature and the aforesaid aspect is to be considered during trial.
It is also required to be noted that the first suit was filed by Munni Devi and thereafter subsequent suit came to be filed by the accused and that too for permanent injunction only.
Nothing is on record that any suit for specific performance has been filed.
Be that as it may, all the aforesaid aspects are required to be considered at the time of trial only.
